title: withOutputSuffix splits on last '.' in whole path, not basename
detail: bun-apps/pi-agent-flux2/src/scenePipeline.ts withOutputSuffix() computes dot = output.lastIndexOf('.') over the FULL path, not just the filename. If a parent directory segment contains a dot (e.g. options.output="/out.v2/render", no extension on filename) with scenePipeline.seeds set, the per-seed suffix (e.g. "_seed5") gets spliced into the middle of the directory name instead of before the filename extension, producing a nonexistent output dir like "/out_seed5.v2/render". Verified directly: {output:"/out.v2/render"} -> {output:"/out_seed5.v2/render"}. Fix: split only on the basename (path.basename/path.dirname or lastIndexOf('/') then '.').

title: runFlux2 can report post-repair output path with pre-repair gate verdict
detail: bun-apps/pi-agent-flux2/src/index.ts runFlux2(): finalOutput correctly falls back to pipeline.handRepair?.output ?? pipeline.winnerOutput (pre-repair winner image when hand-repair produced no output), but the very next field, gate: pipeline.handRepair ? pipeline.handRepair.gate : pipeline.winnerGate, only checks TRUTHINESS of the handRepair object itself -- not whether it actually produced an output/gate. Since scenePipeline.ts sets handRepair = {output:null, gate:null} (still a truthy object) whenever the repair rerender throws or fails to parse its own gate JSON, this branch returns null instead of falling back to pipeline.winnerGate. Net effect: details.output correctly points at the pre-repair, gate-verified winner image, but details.gate is wrongly reported as null/unknown for that same image, even though its real verdict (e.g. PASS or WARN) is already known and available as pipeline.winnerGate. Any caller gating on details.gate (strictGate checks, auto-accept/reject, chained upscale) loses the accurate quality signal for the exact image it is about to use. Confirmed twice via independent review passes against the current code shape (ternary on object truthiness, not on the presence of output/gate fields) -- this is a stable, reproducible defect, not a one-off scenario. Fix: derive output and gate from the same fallback condition (e.g. `const usingRepair = !!pipeline.handRepair?.output; output: usingRepair ? pipeline.handRepair.output : pipeline.winnerOutput; gate: usingRepair ? pipeline.handRepair.gate : pipeline.winnerGate;`).

title: Winner gate re-derived via candidates.find(seed===winnerSeed) instead of reusing pickWinner's chosen object
detail: bun-apps/pi-agent-flux2/src/index.ts's gate: line re-looks-up the winner by seed value (pipeline.candidates.find(c => c.seed === pipeline.winnerSeed)) rather than reusing the actual winning candidate object pickWinner() already selected. Nothing in scenePipeline.ts/the extension validates or dedupes scenePipeline.seeds, so duplicate seeds (e.g. [9,9]) can produce two candidates with the same seed but different gate results; .find() returns the FIRST match (may be the losing one) even though pickWinner correctly tracked the actual best candidate object. Fix: thread the winning candidate object itself through the result instead of re-deriving it by seed lookup.

title: assertPathAllowed accepts a path if EITHER pre-symlink abs OR resolved real path is under an allowed root (OR instead of requiring real-path confinement)
detail: bun-apps/pi-agent-flux2/src/paths.ts assertPathAllowed() uses under(real,root) || under(abs,root) instead of requiring the resolved (real) path to be confined. A symlink planted inside any allowed root (e.g. writable outputDir) can point anywhere on disk (e.g. ~/.ssh/id_rsa) and still validate, because abs (the symlink's own location) is under an allowed root even though real (its target) is not. Reproduced directly: a symlink under outputDir pointing outside repoRoot/outputDir/modelsRoot was accepted instead of throwing. This is a path-traversal / arbitrary file read-or-write escape via staged symlinks. Fix: require under(real, root) unconditionally (only check the resolved path).

title: looksPathy heuristic misclassifies short tokens like ".." as non-path scalars, skipping assertPathAllowed
detail: bun-apps/pi-agent-flux2/src/paths.ts validateExtraArgs()'s looksPathy heuristic (tok.includes('/') || (tok.includes('.') && tok.length > 4)) returns false for ".." (no slash, dot-count check fails length>4), so tokens like ["--output",".."] or ["--models-root",".."] skip assertPathAllowed entirely -- only the leading-dash rejectFlagLike check runs, which ".." also passes. Confirmed by direct repro: validateExtraArgs returned ["--output",".."] unchanged. Since flux2 is spawned with cwd:roots.repoRoot, this resolves outside every allowed root, letting extraArgs write/redirect outside the sandbox. Fix: always run assertPathAllowed on the value token for any allow-listed path-flag, regardless of the looksPathy short-circuit.

title: validateOptionPaths flag-injection guard only checks typeof v === 'string', silently skipping array-typed non-path fields like scene/style's lora: string[]
detail: bun-apps/pi-agent-flux2/src/index.ts validateOptionPaths()'s second loop (rejectFlagLike guard for non-isPath fields) only runs when typeof v === 'string'. Fields declared as string arrays but NOT marked isPath/isPathArray -- concretely lora: string[] on scene/style commands -- are skipped entirely, so an element beginning with '-' (e.g. lora:["legit-lora","--models-root"]) is never checked before buildArgs() emits it as its own argv token. Confirmed by repro: buildArgs produced [...,"--lora","legit-lora","--lora","--models-root"] unrejected. Fix: iterate array elements too when the field is a string array, regardless of isPath status.

title: EXTRA_ARG_ALLOW contains "style-prompt"/"reference-image" which are not real flux2 flags on any command
detail: bun-apps/pi-agent-flux2/src/index.ts EXTRA_ARG_ALLOW allow-lists "style-prompt" and "reference-image", verified against every command's --help output to not exist as real flags. style's override field is actually --prompt (Swift StyleCommand.swift @Option prompt); verify-edit's image field is --image (commands.ts already maps referenceImage -> --image). These look like stale camelCase-derived guesses rather than real flags -- dead allow-list entries widen the extraArgs escape hatch for tokens flux2 never accepts and mislead future readers. Should be pruned; when adding new EXTRA_ARG_ALLOW entries, verify against the actual Swift --help output, not the field's camelCase name.

title: EXTRA_ARG_ALLOW is missing "images", the real --images flag for the edit command
detail: bun-apps/pi-agent-flux2/src/index.ts EXTRA_ARG_ALLOW omits "images" even though --images is edit's real, fully-modeled flag (confirmed live via `flux2 edit --help` and commands.ts's own images field). Calling command:"edit" with extraArgs:["--images","..."] throws PathSafetyError: flag "--images" is not allow-listed, even though it's legitimate. It is the one modeled flag that fell out of sync with EXTRA_ARG_ALLOW -- whenever commands.ts gains/renames a flag, EXTRA_ARG_ALLOW must be updated in the same change.

title: edit command's images field declared isPath:true but Swift --images actually takes ONE comma-separated multi-path string
detail: bun-apps/pi-agent-flux2/src/commands.ts declares edit's images field isPath:true (single-path semantics), but EditCommand.swift does images.split(separator:",") -- the flag takes one comma-joined string of multiple ref paths. index.ts validateOptionPaths calls assertPathAllowed(String(v),...,{mustExist:true}) on the WHOLE comma-joined string, so a genuine multi-ref call like "/repo/a.png,/repo/b.png" fails existsSync() on the literal concatenated string and is rejected with PathSafetyError -- the documented multi-ref use case cannot pass validation at all. Meanwhile a single-path value skips any per-path check a comma-joined string's 2nd+ path might need. Fix: model this field as isPathArray with a comma-split, not isPath.

title: Unguarded awaits in scenePipeline's per-seed loop / VLM verify / hand-repair rerender throw away already-completed work on any failure
detail: bun-apps/pi-agent-flux2/src/scenePipeline.ts has three unguarded await call sites with no try/catch: (1) runSceneOnce inside the per-seed render loop -- can throw synchronously from validateOptionPaths/PathSafetyError or swift build failures unrelated to the flux2 CLI exit code, aborting the whole loop and discarding already-rendered+gated earlier-seed candidates; (2) askAboutImage VLM verification -- pi-vlm's askImage (bun-apps/pi-vlm/src/vlm/ask.ts) only wraps session.prompt in try/catch, NOT readFileSync(abs) or createSharedSession, so a not-yet-flushed image or LM Studio being down throws instead of resolving {ok:false}, propagating uncaught through vlm.ts's askAboutImage (which adds no defensive catch of its own) and killing the entire multi-seed pipeline; (3) the post-winner hand-repair rerender -- by this point winnerSeed/winnerOutput/candidates are already fully valid, but a crash/rejection here discards the entire ScenePipelineResult instead of degrading gracefully to the already-found winner with handRepair:null. Fix: wrap each of these three call sites in try/catch and degrade to partial-progress results (mark ok:false for that seed/step) rather than letting the pipeline throw.

title: Live e2e baseline (LM Studio available): t2i/upscale-chain/scene-pipeline(no-vlm)/scene-pipeline(vlm)/gate all PASS
detail: With lmStudioAvailable=true, all 5 live-e2e steps returned ok:true across two independent runs: t2i (gate=PASS), upscale-chain (gate=PASS), scene-pipeline-no-vlm (winnerReason=best-gate, seeds 11&22 both PASS), scene-pipeline-vlm (winnerReason=verify-match, both candidates PASS with matching VLM replies), gate (PASS). Reproduced again on 2026-07-01T19-39-52 with identical shape (winnerReason values, gate=PASS for all steps). Use this as the reference baseline when checking for live-e2e regressions in future runs of this workflow.

title: Contract lane baseline: test count grew from 64->131 (6->11 files) as the module matured; 18/18 commands stay fully modeled with no CLI-flag drift
detail: 2026-07-01T18-52-16 baseline: testsSummary="64 pass / 0 fail across 6 files (149 expect() calls)". 2026-07-01T19-39-52 rerun: testsSummary="131 pass / 0 fail across 11 files (315 expect() calls, 252.00ms)" -- test suite roughly doubled in files/assertions (new coverage added between runs), still 0 fail. checkFlagsSummary stayed "18/18 commands fully modeled. No drift." both times (only the checkmark glyph/warning-line wording varied cosmetically: "✓ No drift." vs "No drift."). Use the LATEST numbers (131/11/315) as the current reference baseline for pi-agent-flux2's contract lane; a drop in pass count/file count relative to the most recent run, or reappearance of drift warning lines, signals a regression worth investigating before merging schema/commands.ts changes.

title: Multi-seed render loop never checks the caller's AbortSignal between iterations, so cancelling mid-run still renders every remaining seed
detail: bun-apps/pi-agent-flux2/src/scenePipeline.ts's for-loop over pipelineOpts.seeds has no `if (signal?.aborted) break;` check. invokeFlux2 (invoke.ts) kills the in-flight child process when signal fires and RESOLVES rather than throws, so the for-loop sees no exception and proceeds to call deps.runSceneOnce for every remaining seed -- each spawns a new flux2 child that invoke.ts immediately kills again (signal already aborted), burning process-spawn overhead and wall-clock time on every remaining seed instead of returning immediately after abort. Defeats the purpose of passing an AbortSignal into a multi-seed pipeline (e.g. runFlux2({command:'scene', scenePipeline:{seeds:[1,2,3,4,5]}, signal}) aborted while seed 1 renders still spawns+kills seeds 2-5). Fix: check signal?.aborted at the top of each loop iteration and break early.

title: Model-selector fields (transformer/vae/encoder/tokenizerDir/lora/model) are validated only by rejectFlagLike, never assertPathAllowed, letting '../' escape the sandbox into ModelPaths roots
detail: bun-apps/pi-agent-flux2/src/index.ts's validateOptionPaths + commands.ts's GEN_FIELDS never mark transformer/vae/encoder/tokenizerDir/lora/model as isPath, so pathFieldKeys(spec) skips them and only the generic rejectFlagLike (leading-dash) check runs. Meanwhile the Swift side (Flux2ModelRegistry / T2ICommand.swift and EditCommand/SceneCommand/StyleCommand/AngleCommand/SwapCommand/ExpandCommand/StoryCommand/UpscaleCommand.swift) does raw ModelPaths.{transformerRoot,vaeRoot,textEncoderRoot,tokenizerRoot,loraRoot,upscaleRoot}.appendingPathComponent(value) with NO '..'-sanitization. Confirmed: calling t2i/scene/edit/etc with options.transformer="../../../../../../etc" passes rejectFlagLike (no leading dash) and buildArgs emits it unchanged; Swift then walks '..' entirely outside mlx-models/transformer to an attacker-chosen absolute location, defeating the allowed-roots sandbox assertPathAllowed is supposed to enforce. Same class applies to lora (string[], loraRoot.appendingPathComponent(name)) and model on upscale (upscaleRoot.appendingPathComponent(model)), and the equivalent fields on verify-* diagnostic commands. Distinct from the lora flag-injection gap (flux2-index:array-field-skips-flag-injection-check, which only covers leading-dash tokens) -- this is full '..' path-traversal on ALL model-selector fields, path or not. Fix: mark these fields isPath/isPathArray and run assertPathAllowed with the correct allowed root (modelsRoot subpaths), or at minimum reject any value containing '..' path segments.

title: GEN_FIELDS.strictGate is spread into t2i/edit/style/angle but only scene/upscale actually implement --strict-gate on the Swift side
detail: bun-apps/pi-agent-flux2/src/commands.ts unconditionally spreads `...GEN_FIELDS` (which includes strictGate) into t2i/edit/style/angle, but T2ICommand/EditCommand/StyleCommand/AngleCommand.swift never declare --strict-gate -- confirmed live via `flux2 <cmd> --help`: only scene and upscale expose it. The tool schema and extensions/pi-flux2.ts's generated fieldHints doc (iterates COMMANDS) advertise strictGate as valid for all 4, with no per-command caveat in the tool description ("Set options.strictGate true to abort on a FAIL gate"). Calling command:'t2i' with options:{prompt:'x', strictGate:true} emits `--strict-gate`; verified directly that the real binary exits 1 with "Error: Unknown option '--strict-gate'" for t2i. A documented, schema-valid option deterministically breaks these 4 commands. Fix: remove strictGate from t2i/edit/style/angle's field set (or add it to those Swift commands if the feature is actually wanted there).

title: swap spreads full GEN_FIELDS (cfgScale/vae/encoder/tokenizerDir/strictGate) and upscale spreads GEN_FIELDS_BARE (transformer/seed/vae/encoder/tokenizerDir), but SwapCommand.swift/UpscaleCommand.swift implement none of those flags
detail: commands.ts: swap spreads `...GEN_FIELDS` even though `flux2 swap --help` lists only source/reference/prompt/threshold/feather/mask-dilate/preserve-aspect-ratio/inpaint/harmonize/transformer/seed/width/height/steps/output/output-dir/name/no-artifacts -- cfgScale/vae/encoder/tokenizerDir/strictGate are pure schema drift. Verified directly: `--vae flux2-klein` on swap exits with "Error: Unknown option '--vae'. Did you mean '--name'?". Separately, upscale spreads GEN_FIELDS_BARE which still carries transformer/seed/vae/encoder/tokenizerDir even though UpscaleCommand.swift is a pure ESRGAN pass (`flux2 upscale --help` only has models-root/input/model/tile-size/tile-overlap/no-tile/output/output-dir/name/no-artifacts/strict-gate) -- verified `--seed 42` on upscale exits 1 with "Error: Unknown option '--seed'". Both are schema-valid per commands.ts and appear in the tool's per-command field reference, so an agent following the documented schema for either command will deterministically hit an unknown-option crash on 5+ modeled-but-nonexistent fields. Fix: give swap/upscale their own narrow field sets instead of spreading the generic GEN_FIELDS/GEN_FIELDS_BARE blocks.

title: scenePipeline requests dynamically import("./vlm.ts") + resolveVlmLLM() unconditionally, even when verifyPrompt is omitted (no VLM needed at all)
detail: bun-apps/pi-agent-flux2/src/index.ts runs `const vlm = await import('./vlm.ts'); const llm = vlm.resolveVlmLLM(input.scenePipeline.vlmModel);` unconditionally for every scenePipeline request, BEFORE checking whether input.scenePipeline.verifyPrompt is even set -- i.e. even for a pure gate-based multi-seed pick (the 'scene-pipeline-no-vlm' e2e baseline case) that intentionally has zero LM Studio/pi-vlm dependency. This throw happens synchronously outside any try/catch in index.ts or scenePipeline.ts, so in a standalone/bundled binary where pi-vlm isn't bundled/resolvable, or if @earendil-works/pi-coding-agent's AuthStorage/ModelRegistry import throws in that environment, the ENTIRE multi-seed render aborts (zero candidates produced, zero partial gate results) even though the requested pipeline never needed a VLM. Contradicts the module's own JSDoc promise that 'Non-zero flux2 exit is NOT an exception -- it surfaces as details.ok=false' and violates the reusable-library contract implied for a future CLI command. Related to but distinct from flux2-scenepipeline:unguarded-external-calls-lose-partial-progress (that record covers askAboutImage failing WHEN verifyPrompt IS used; this one covers the vlm module even being touched when verifyPrompt is NOT used). Fix: gate the `import('./vlm.ts')` + resolveVlmLLM call behind `if (input.scenePipeline.verifyPrompt) { ... }`, or wrap it in try/catch and degrade to a no-VLM pipeline on failure.
